title: Netherlands Takes EU Aviation Lead As Amsterdam Helps Commercial Flights Reach 6.9 Million
description:
Eurostat, on 28 August 2026, released the rise of EU commercial flights, which increased by 3.8 percent to 6.9 million.
The latest Eurostat commercial flight data show that Schiphol recorded approximately 488,000 scheduled and non-scheduled commercial flights.
EU Commercial Flights Rise By 3.8 Per Cent Eurostat recorded 6.9 million commercial flights across the EU in 2025.
Amsterdam Schiphol was the busiest EU airport by commercial flight movements in 2025, with 488,000 flights.
Across the EU, commercial flights were 3.8% higher than in 2025 at 6.9 million.
text:
The Netherlands leads the rest of the EU countries after Schiphol Airport in Amsterdam reported a total of 488,000 commercial flights in 2025. Eurostat, on 28 August 2026, released the rise of EU commercial flights, which increased by 3.8 percent to 6.9 million. Charles de Gaulle in Paris came in second place with 476,000 flights, while Frankfurt Main reported 457,000 flights. While flight statistics have only reached about 2019 levels, air transport links continue to play a major role in the travel, trade, and accessibility of the EU. European airports and airlines still face challenges of balancing the demand for air transport against the resilience and environmental sustainability of the industry.

Netherlands Leads EU Aviation Recovery Through Amsterdam Schiphol

The Netherlands has emerged at the front of Europe’s commercial flight recovery, with Amsterdam Schiphol handling more aircraft movements than any other airport in the European Union during 2025.

The latest Eurostat commercial flight data show that Schiphol recorded approximately 488,000 scheduled and non-scheduled commercial flights. Paris Charles de Gaulle ranked second with 476,000 flights, while Frankfurt Main followed with 457,000.

These figures establish Amsterdam as the EU leader by commercial aircraft movements. They do not mean that Amsterdam handled the highest number of passengers.

Paris Charles de Gaulle remained the EU’s busiest airport by passenger volume in 2024. The distinction matters because one aircraft movement can carry very different numbers of passengers depending on the route, aircraft size, load factor and operating model.

The new figures nevertheless underline Schiphol’s central position within the European aviation network. Amsterdam connects short-haul European markets with long-haul destinations across North America, Asia, Africa and the Middle East.

EU Commercial Flights Rise By 3.8 Per Cent

Eurostat recorded 6.9 million commercial flights across the EU in 2025. That represented an increase of 3.8 per cent from the 6.7 million registered in 2024.

Commercial flight activity has increased continuously since 2021. By 2025, the annual total had returned to approximately the same level as the seven million flights recorded in 2019.

The EU aviation recovery is therefore substantial but not an expansion far beyond the pre-pandemic benchmark. Total movements have returned to roughly their previous scale after years of disruption and uneven rebuilding.

This distinction supports a measured interpretation. Europe’s aviation system has recovered its operational volume, but the headline figure alone does not prove that every airport, airline or regional market has recovered equally.

Amsterdam Extends Its Lead Over Paris And Frankfurt

Amsterdam Schiphol also ranked first for commercial flight movements in 2024, when it handled approximately 484,000 flights. Paris Charles de Gaulle recorded 463,000, while Frankfurt Main handled 437,000.

The 2025 results indicate that all three leading hubs increased their movement totals.

Amsterdam retained first place, but Paris and Frankfurt added more movements in absolute terms. Frankfurt recorded the largest increase among the three airports, although it remained third in the overall ranking.

That pattern shows why the word “leads” is more accurate than “overtakes”. Schiphol already held the highest position in 2024 and maintained it in 2025.

Flight Movements And Passenger Numbers Tell Different Stories

Commercial flight rankings should not be confused with passenger rankings. An airport can handle more flights but fewer passengers when it operates a larger share of regional services, smaller aircraft or routes with lower average loads.

Official Eurostat air passenger statistics show that approximately 1.1 billion passengers travelled by air in the EU during 2024, an increase of 8.3 per cent from 2023.

Paris Charles de Gaulle handled 70.3 million passengers in 2024. Amsterdam Schiphol received 66.8 million, while Madrid Barajas recorded 66.1 million and Frankfurt Main handled 61.5 million.

Amsterdam consequently led the EU in commercial aircraft movements, while Paris led in passengers handled. Both measures are important, but they answer different questions.

Flight numbers reveal the intensity of airport and airspace activity. Passenger totals show the volume of people moving through the system.

Summer Demand Drives Europe’s Busiest Flight Period

Eurostat identified June, July and August as the busiest months for commercial flight activity in 2025. August led with 693,046 flights, narrowly ahead of July with 690,855.

June recorded 648,707 flights. These months also accounted for the highest numbers of non-scheduled services, including charter and other special commercial operations.

This seasonal concentration reflects the importance of summer leisure travel across Europe. Mediterranean destinations, island markets and major cultural cities experience particularly strong demand during the main holiday season.

The figures also highlight a capacity challenge. Airports, airlines, border agencies, ground handlers and air traffic services must manage their heaviest workloads within a relatively short period.

Travel businesses depend on this peak. Hotels, attractions, coach operators, cruise ports, restaurants and destination companies often generate a large share of their annual revenue during the European summer.

Charter Flights Strengthen Seasonal Tourism Links

Non-scheduled commercial services represented 8.5 per cent of all EU flights in 2025. This category includes charter flights, air taxis, sightseeing services, offshore operations and other commercial services that do not follow a conventional published schedule.

Among the ten EU airports with the highest flight totals, Athens International Airport recorded the largest non-scheduled share at 5.2 per cent. Madrid Barajas followed at 4.8 per cent, while Copenhagen Kastrup recorded 4.1 per cent.

Charter traffic remains important to package holidays and organised leisure travel. It allows tour operators to add seasonal capacity to destinations where demand rises sharply for part of the year.

The segment is especially relevant to:

Mediterranean beach destinations

Island tourism markets

Winter sun programmes

Ski and mountain holidays

Cruise embarkation cities

Large sporting and cultural events

Special-interest group travel

A higher charter share does not automatically indicate stronger total tourism performance. It shows that non-scheduled operations play a more visible role within an airport’s traffic mix.

Strong Aviation Access Supports European Tourism

Europe’s aviation recovery coincides with continued strength in its visitor economy. Eurostat recorded more than three billion nights in EU tourist accommodation during 2024, supported by growth in international demand.

Spain remained the largest EU destination for international guest nights. Italy, France, Greece and Austria also held leading positions.

The connection between aviation and tourism is particularly strong for islands and destinations located far from major source markets. Air services allow visitors to reach Mediterranean beaches, historic cities, mountain areas and regional destinations within practical journey times.

However, the 6.9 million flight total cannot be converted directly into visitor arrivals or tourism receipts. Commercial flights also carry residents, business travellers, people visiting friends and relatives, freight and mail.

The official flight dataset does not measure:

The number of tourists on each flight

Average visitor spending

Hotel occupancy generated by aviation

Tourism revenue attributable to airports

Employment created by the additional movements

The purpose of every passenger’s journey

Any economic analysis must therefore combine aviation statistics with passenger, accommodation, spending and labour-market data.

Airlines Gain Scale But Continue To Face Operational Pressure

More commercial flights expand the number of seats and connections available across the European market. Airlines can rebuild frequencies, strengthen hub banks and respond to seasonal demand.

A larger schedule can also improve connectivity for smaller cities. Travellers from regional airports may gain access to long-haul destinations through hubs such as Amsterdam, Paris and Frankfurt.

Yet the operating environment remains demanding. Airlines must balance passenger demand with airport capacity, air traffic management constraints, labour availability, fuel costs and environmental requirements.

Dense hub schedules also increase exposure to disruption. A delayed inbound aircraft can affect passenger connections, crew rotations and later departures across an airline’s network.

The rise in movements therefore creates opportunities and operational responsibilities. Reliable performance matters as much as the number of flights offered.

Airports Face Capacity And Passenger-Service Tests

Amsterdam Schiphol’s leading position places significant demands on terminal systems, runways, baggage operations, security processing and ground handling.

Paris Charles de Gaulle and Frankfurt face similar pressures. Each airport operates as a gateway for its national market and as a transfer hub for international passengers.

When flight volumes approach pre-pandemic levels, airports must ensure that infrastructure and staffing can manage busy periods without undermining passenger service.

Priority areas include:

Security and border-processing capacity

Baggage reliability

Passenger assistance

Transfer times

Terminal crowd management

Surface transport connections

Weather resilience

Disruption communication

Airport performance influences the wider visitor experience. A traveller’s first and last impressions of a destination are often shaped by immigration queues, baggage delivery and transport from the terminal.

Regional Airports Remain Important To Tourism Distribution

Major hubs dominate the latest ranking, but regional airports remain essential to Europe’s visitor economy. They connect travellers directly with coastal areas, heritage cities, rural regions and islands.

Direct access can distribute tourism spending beyond national capitals. It can also reduce the need for long ground transfers from a distant hub.

Regional services support hotels, restaurants, attractions, car-hire companies and local transport operators. They can also help smaller destinations attract events and business travel.

These routes may be more vulnerable to seasonal fluctuations or airline network changes. Local authorities and tourism organisations consequently need to base route-development decisions on credible demand, economic value and long-term viability.

The latest Eurostat release does not provide a regional tourism impact assessment. It does, however, show that the broader European network has regained a level of activity close to 2019.

Hotels And Tour Operators Benefit From Wider Connectivity

Flight availability shapes the number of destinations that tour operators can sell and the length of stay they can offer. Greater frequency gives travellers more flexibility over departure dates and trip duration.

Hotels can benefit when improved access creates additional demand. Airport hotels, city accommodation and properties near major attractions may gain from both leisure and business traffic.

Tour operators also use charter flights and reserved seat allocations to build complete packages. These arrangements can support predictable visitor flows during peak periods.

The benefits are not automatic. Accommodation providers still depend on pricing, destination appeal, consumer confidence, local events and the availability of skilled workers.

Higher aviation activity may increase the pool of potential visitors, but it does not guarantee equal gains for every destination or tourism business.

Local Economies Depend On Reliable International Access

Amsterdam, Paris and Frankfurt are not only transfer points. They are major destinations with extensive hotel, cultural, retail, conference and hospitality sectors.

International access supports corporate meetings, exhibitions, academic travel, cultural events and city breaks. It also connects businesses with customers, investors and skilled workers.

Tourism industries employed approximately 13.4 million people across the EU business economy in 2023, according to Eurostat. The sector included around 2.7 million enterprises, many of them small or medium-sized businesses.

Tourism industries accounted for 8.3 per cent of people employed in the EU business economy and 4.9 per cent of its value added. These figures describe the wider tourism sector and must not be presented as the direct result of the 2025 flight increase.

Reliable air connectivity nevertheless remains an important part of the operating environment for these businesses.

Sustainability Becomes Central To Aviation Growth

The return of commercial flight volumes to near-2019 levels increases attention on aviation emissions, local air quality and noise around airports.

The European Union is implementing ReFuelEU Aviation to increase the share of sustainable aviation fuel supplied at EU airports. The policy forms part of the Fit for 55 package and supports the EU’s target of reducing net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55 per cent by 2030.

The European Commission’s ReFuelEU Aviation framework requires fuel suppliers to increase the proportion of sustainable aviation fuel blended with conventional aviation fuel.

The mandated share began at 2 per cent in 2025 and rises to 6 per cent in 2030. Longer-term requirements extend towards 2050.

Sustainable fuel is not the only measure under consideration. More efficient aircraft, improved air traffic management, better ground operations and stronger rail-air integration can also contribute to reducing aviation’s environmental impact.

Netherlands Must Balance Connectivity With Airport Impacts

Schiphol’s role brings significant connectivity benefits to the Netherlands. It also creates difficult questions involving noise, emissions, airport capacity and the quality of life in surrounding communities.

The movement ranking does not assess whether 488,000 flights represent the optimal level for the airport. It simply records the commercial operations completed during 2025.

Decisions about future capacity remain subject to Dutch and European rules, environmental assessments and consultation processes.

This means Schiphol’s position should not be framed only as a competition between countries. Airport policy must consider passengers, airlines, residents, tourism businesses and environmental commitments.

The challenge is to preserve useful connectivity while improving operational performance and limiting harmful effects.

What The Recovery Means For International Travellers

The return of EU flight activity to near-2019 levels can provide travellers with greater choice across major European gateways.

More frequencies may offer:

A wider choice of departure times

Better connections through major hubs

More direct regional links

Greater access to seasonal destinations

Additional competition on selected routes

Improved options after cancellations

Travellers should still avoid assuming that higher network activity guarantees lower fares or fewer delays. Ticket prices depend on demand, operating costs, taxes, competition and the timing of booking.

Passengers connecting through Amsterdam, Paris or Frankfurt should check the minimum connection time shown by their airline. They should also monitor terminal information because gates and departure areas can change.

Future Outlook Based On Official European Policy

Official data show that commercial flight activity increased every year from 2021 to 2025. The total has now returned to approximately its 2019 scale.

Future aviation development will be shaped by passenger demand, airport capacity and environmental policy. The European Union’s published plans focus on sustainable fuel, lower-carbon transport and efficient connectivity.

The figures do not provide an official forecast for flight growth beyond 2025. It would therefore be premature to claim that movements will continue rising at the same rate.

Amsterdam begins the next phase as the EU airport with the highest commercial flight count. Paris remains the passenger leader, while Frankfurt continues to strengthen its movement total.

The next test will concern quality as much as quantity. Reliability, accessibility, passenger service and environmental performance will determine whether aviation recovery delivers lasting value for travellers and destinations.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Amsterdam Schiphol now the busiest airport in the European Union?

Amsterdam Schiphol was the busiest EU airport by commercial flight movements in 2025, with 488,000 flights. Paris Charles de Gaulle remained the leading EU airport by passenger volume in the latest annual passenger ranking.

Does the 6.9 million figure represent passenger flights only?

No. Eurostat’s total includes scheduled and non-scheduled commercial flights carrying passengers, freight or mail under instrument flight rules. Non-scheduled operations include charter flights, air taxis and other special commercial services.

What should travellers know when connecting through Amsterdam, Paris or Frankfurt?

Travellers should check their airline’s minimum connection time, terminal information and live flight status. They should allow extra time during the busy summer period and keep essential documents, medication and valuables in their hand luggage.

Conclusion

The Netherlands maintained its position as Europe’s leader for commercial flight operations in 2025, with Amsterdam Schiphol handling 488,000 movements, compared to Paris Charles de Gaulle and Frankfurt Main. Across the EU, commercial flights were 3.8% higher than in 2025 at 6.9 million. This is expected to be a good sign of operations returning back to their pre-pandemic levels. However, the numbers show that the aviation sector is facing new challenges. Airlines and airports must work on improving their infrastructure and passenger service while also meeting new environmental standards. A continuous improvement of services will also help tourism by making more connections available to various locations. However, the potential of these improvements will only be realized with improvements in sustainability and resilient operations.

text:
India’s sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) industry could reach cost parity with conventional jet fuel by 2036, according to a report. The shift could become possible through domestic SAF production, agricultural residue and low-cost renewable power. The report also says the gap may close earlier if the wider benefits of cleaner fuel, such as lower pollution and reduced crop burning, are included while assessing its economic value.

Why Is SAF More Expensive Now?

Sustainable aviation fuel is seen as an important option for making air travel cleaner, but its cost remains a major challenge.

The report by Gulf Times said comparing SAF with conventional jet fuel on the basis of one year's production cost does not show the complete picture. SAF projects are expected to operate for many years, so their costs need to be studied over a longer period.

Power-and-biomass-to-liquids, or PBtL fuel, is estimated to cost around $1.42 per litre in 2030. Conventional jet fuel, by comparison, is estimated at about $0.97 per litre.

The difference looks significant at first. Over a 25-year project period, however, the gap becomes much smaller.

What Could Happen by 2036?

Researchers estimated that a PBtL plant commissioned in 2030 could have a levelised cost of around Rs 127 per litre. This would be about 18 per cent higher than the adjusted long-term purchase cost of conventional jet fuel.

The numbers become more encouraging for projects starting later. Under the report's base-case assumptions, new synthetic fuel facilities commissioned in 2036 could reach full cost parity with conventional jet fuel.

In simple terms, SAF may no longer carry a major cost disadvantage by then.

That could be an important change for airlines and fuel producers. Cheaper SAF would make it easier for the aviation industry to use more sustainable fuel without taking on a much higher fuel bill.

How Can India Reduce Fuel Risks?

India's fuel costs are affected by global crude prices and movements in the rupee against the US dollar. The report pointed to this as another reason why domestic SAF production could become useful.

Between 2005 and 2025, wholesale jet fuel prices increased by around 5 per cent every year in nominal rupee terms. Around 1.9 per cent of this increase was linked to US dollar commodity inflation, while 3.1 per cent came from rupee depreciation against the dollar.

Domestic synthetic fuel plants could reduce some of this currency risk. Major operating inputs, particularly electricity, can potentially be secured through long-term power purchase agreements in rupees at fixed tariffs.

That gives producers more control over future costs.

Can Farm Waste Help Aviation?

One of India's biggest advantages could be its agricultural residue.

Crop waste is available in large quantities across the country. Instead of being burned in fields, some of this material could be used as a feedstock for sustainable aviation fuel.

This could create benefits beyond aviation. Less field burning can help reduce air pollution and improve public health.

The report estimated that the health benefits from lower agricultural burning could represent around $0.38 per litre in avoided social costs. Carbon costs could add another benefit of up to $0.22 per litre.

These figures could make SAF look more attractive when its wider economic value is considered.

Could SAF Reach Parity Before 2036?

The report says it is possible. If environmental and social benefits are included in policy decisions, commercial cost parity could potentially arrive as early as 2030.

That does not mean SAF will automatically become cheaper by that year. Much will depend on investment, technology, renewable electricity costs, feedstock availability and government policy.

Still, the long-term outlook is becoming more interesting for India.

A strong domestic SAF industry could help reduce dependence on imported crude oil, limit exposure to foreign exchange movements and give agricultural waste a useful new purpose.

For India's growing aviation sector, that could make sustainable aviation fuel much more than a cleaner alternative. It could become a practical part of the country's future energy strategy.

JINAN, China, 30. August 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Die Niutech Technology Group Co., Ltd. (im Folgenden „Niutech"), ein globaler Anbieter von industriellen Lösungen für die kontinuierliche Pyrolyse, hat mit einem weltweit führenden Energiekonzern einen Kaufvertrag über eine industrielle Produktionsanlage zur kontinuierlichen Pyrolyse von Kunststoffabfällen unterzeichnet. Sie wird eine der Großraffinerien des Kunden modernisieren und eine durchgängige Produktion vom Pyrolyseöl aus Kunststoffabfällen bis hin zu hydriertem Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) ermöglichen. Dies ist Niutechs erster Einstieg in die Lieferkette des Kunden.

text:
Từ những chai dầu ăn đã qua sử dụng trong căn bếp gia đình, Nhật Bản đang xây dựng chuỗi sản xuất nhiên liệu hàng không bền vững (SAF) nhằm giảm phát thải carbon. Tuy nhiên, để biến tham vọng ấy thành hiện thực, quốc gia này vẫn phải vượt qua nhiều rào cản về nguồn nguyên liệu và chi phí sản xuất.

Từ căn bếp đến bầu trời

Trong căn bếp nhỏ tại Tokyo (Nhật Bản), chị Maki Watanabe cẩn thận rót dầu ăn thừa sau khi chiên vào chai nhựa thay vì đổ bỏ. Mỗi năm, chị đóng góp khoảng 40 lít dầu đã qua sử dụng cho chương trình tái chế quốc gia.

Thói quen ấy là một mắt xích trong chiến lược phát triển nhiên liệu hàng không bền vững (Sustainable Aviation Fuel – SAF), loại nhiên liệu được kỳ vọng giúp ngành hàng không giảm phát thải carbon.

Nhật Bản đặt mục tiêu đến năm 2030 thay thế khoảng 10% nhiên liệu máy bay truyền thống bằng SAF, tương đương 1,7 triệu kilolít mỗi năm. Với một quốc gia hạn chế tài nguyên, tận dụng dầu ăn đã qua sử dụng được xem là giải pháp vừa tăng cường an ninh năng lượng, vừa giảm phát thải.

SAF có thể được sản xuất từ dầu ăn đã qua sử dụng, phụ phẩm nông nghiệp, rác thải sinh hoạt hoặc tảo. Trong đó, dầu ăn thải được đánh giá là nguồn nguyên liệu khả thi nhất nhờ nguồn cung sẵn có và quy trình xử lý hoàn thiện. Tùy công nghệ sản xuất, SAF có thể giảm tới 80% lượng phát thải khí nhà kính so với nhiên liệu hàng không truyền thống.

Để bảo đảm nguồn nguyên liệu, Nhật Bản triển khai chương trình hợp tác công - tư với khoảng 300 doanh nghiệp và tổ chức. Dầu ăn đã qua sử dụng được thu gom tại siêu thị, cửa hàng tiện lợi và các điểm tập kết trước khi đưa đến nhà máy sản xuất SAF.

Nhiều địa phương cũng xây dựng chuỗi cung ứng khép kín. Tại thành phố Shimonoseki, dầu ăn được thu gom từ hộ gia đình và doanh nghiệp, rồi chuyển đến nhà máy Cosmo Oil để tinh chế thành SAF, góp phần giảm phụ thuộc vào nguyên liệu nhập khẩu.

Khoảng cách đến mục tiêu 2030

Dù được đánh giá là một trong những quốc gia đi đầu châu Á về phát triển SAF, Nhật Bản vẫn đối mặt với khoảng cách lớn giữa mục tiêu và năng lực sản xuất thực tế.

Thách thức lớn nhất là nguồn nguyên liệu. Nhật Bản đã thu gom gần như toàn bộ dầu ăn thải từ nhà hàng và doanh nghiệp, nên phần còn lại phụ thuộc chủ yếu vào các hộ gia đình. Tuy nhiên, trong năm tài chính 2024, Tokyo chỉ thu được khoảng 160 kilolít dầu ăn từ khu dân cư, thấp hơn nhiều so với tiềm năng.

Để cải thiện tình hình, chính quyền Tokyo phát miễn phí 13.000 phễu nhựa có mã QR hướng dẫn thu gom và đặt mục tiêu tiếp cận khoảng 7,8 triệu hộ gia đình. Nhiều doanh nghiệp như Fujifilm, Aeon, Ito-Yokado và 7-Eleven cũng mở thêm các điểm thu gom tại căng tin và cửa hàng bán lẻ.

Bên cạnh đó, chi phí sản xuất SAF vẫn là rào cản lớn. Quá trình thu gom, vận chuyển, xử lý và tinh chế đòi hỏi vốn đầu tư cao, trong khi nhu cầu thị trường chưa đủ ổn định, khiến nhiều doanh nghiệp còn thận trọng.

Dù vậy, áp lực chuyển đổi sang SAF đang gia tăng trên toàn cầu. Liên minh châu Âu yêu cầu pha trộn tối thiểu 2% SAF từ năm 2025; Singapore sẽ áp dụng phụ phí SAF đối với vé máy bay từ năm 2026, còn Hàn Quốc và Thái Lan cũng đang xây dựng các quy định tương tự.

Theo ông Tadashi Okada - Giám đốc Tiếp thị Nhà máy lọc dầu Cosmo Oil, việc biến dầu ăn đã qua sử dụng thành nhiên liệu hàng không không chỉ góp phần tái chế tài nguyên, thúc đẩy nền kinh tế carbon thấp mà còn cần sự tham gia rộng rãi của cộng đồng trong phân loại, thu gom dầu ăn thải ngay từ mỗi gia đình.

text:
New Delhi, Aug 29 (IANS) The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has prohibited the sale of compounded asafoetida (hing powder) by Everest Food Products Private Limited and Laljee Godhoo over alleged non-compliance with prescribed food safety standards, the regulator said on Saturday.

Taking to the social media platform X, the food safety regulator said it had issued prohibition orders against the two firms under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, following surveillance and legal sampling that found compounded hing products to be sub-standard and, in some cases, misbranded or adulterated.

In the case of Everest Food Products, samples of compounded asafoetida (hing powder) and its variants were found to be misbranded and sub-standard by the Food Analyst of the primary food laboratory.

FSSAI said the alcohol-soluble extract in one sample was found to be 0 per cent against the prescribed minimum standard of 5 per cent. Samples of Yellow Hing Powder and Black Hing Powder were also found to be sub-standard, with alcoholic extract levels of 3.29 per cent and 4.4 per cent, respectively.

The regulator said routine surveillance had also found non-compliance with the prescribed alcoholic extract parameter.

Previous regulatory compliance reviews of products including Chicken Masala, Garam Masala and Egg Curry Powder had also identified labelling-related non-compliances, it added.

FSSAI said consistent non-compliance had been observed in samples of asafoetida collected from various sources and locations, with products found to contain less than the prescribed 5 per cent alcoholic extract.

The sale of compounded asafoetida with all its variants by Everest Food Products has therefore been prohibited with immediate effect until further orders.

In the case of Laljee Godhoo, samples of compounded hing and compounded asafoetida, in powder and lump forms, were found to be sub-standard and not conforming to prescribed requirements.

Raw hing varieties used in manufacturing the compounded product were also found to be sub-standard due to excess starch. FSSAI regulations prescribe that starch content in hing should not exceed 1 per cent by weight.

The regulator said the violations were considered pervasive across batches based on market surveillance, legal sampling and test reports of raw materials.

Both firms have been directed to submit action plans for rectification and ensure that only standard products are manufactured and sold. FSSAI said further action would be initiated under the law if satisfactory compliance is not established.

Ziel der Kooperation ist die Herstellung von nachhaltigem Flugkraftstoff (Sustainable Aviation Fuel, SAF).

Integration in bestehende Raffinerieprozesse

Ein wesentlicher Bestandteil des vereinbarten Projekts ist die Integration einer Raffinerie-Upgrade-Lösung. Dabei wird das durch das kontinuierliche Pyrolyseverfahren gewonnene Öl in einem weiteren Schritt zu hydriertem SAF veredelt. Dieser Prozess ermöglicht es, Kunststoffabfälle, die andernfalls schwer zu recyceln wären, als Rohstoffquelle für den Luftverkehr nutzbar zu machen.

Die technologische Entwicklung steht im Kontext verschärfter regulatorischer Anforderungen in Europa. Die Mandate der Europäischen Union sehen verbindliche Beimischungsquoten für nachhaltige Kraftstoffe vor.

Demnach müssen ab dem kommenden Jahr 2025 mindestens 2 % des Flugkraftstoffs aus nachhaltigen Quellen stammen. Diese Quote soll bis zum Jahr 2030 auf 6 % steigen und bis zur Mitte des Jahrhunderts, im Jahr 2050, einen Anteil von 70 % erreichen.

Marktumfeld und technologische Skalierung

Anzeige

Die EU verschärft die SAF-Pflicht: Ab 2026 steigen die Quoten rasant – bis 2050 auf 70 Prozent. Wer jetzt die Technologie versteht, sichert sich strategische Vorteile. Dieser Report zeigt, wie Pyrolyse-Anlagen die Lücke füllen und was das für Ihre Investitionsplanung bedeutet. Jetzt kostenlosen SAF-Report anfordern

Die industrielle Skalierung, wie sie das Projekt von Niutech vorsieht, markiert einen wichtigen Schritt in der Branche. Zum Vergleich: Forschungskonsortien wie das Paul Scherrer Institut (PSI) und das Unternehmen Metafuels betreiben derzeit Testanlagen wie „Aerobrew“, die eine tägliche Menge von rund 50 Litern synthetischen Kraftstoffs produzieren.

Für eine geplante Fabrik in Rotterdam strebt Metafuels ab dem Jahr 2030 eine Produktion von 10 Tonnen pro Tag an, die später auf 100 Tonnen pro Tag gesteigert werden soll.

Trotz der technologischen Fortschritte bleibt die wirtschaftliche Komponente eine Herausforderung für die Luftfahrtindustrie. Branchenexperten zufolge kosten nachhaltige Kraftstoffe derzeit etwa das Vier- bis Fünffache von herkömmlichem, fossilem Kerosin.

Anzeige

SAF-Kosten liegen vier- bis fünffach über fossilem Kerosin – ein Risiko für Ihre Kostenstruktur. Doch die neue Pyrolyse-Technologie von Niutech zeigt: Skalierung senkt die Kosten. Erfahren Sie, wie Sie mit dem richtigen Technologiemix Ihre Compliance-Kosten senken und Versorgungssicherheit gewinnen. SAF-Kostenrisiko jetzt minimieren

Die steigenden gesetzlichen Anforderungen an die Beimischung, die für das Jahr 2035 bereits eine Quote von 20 % vorsehen, erhöhen jedoch den Druck auf Energiekonzerne, in großvolumige Produktionskapazitäten zu investieren.

Durch den nun geschlossenen Vertrag über eine Anlage mit einer Kapazität von bis zu 50.000 Tonnen jährlich positioniert sich Niutech als Zulieferer für die industrielle Umsetzung dieser Energiewende im Flugverkehr. Das Projekt unterstreicht den Trend, chemisches Recycling durch Pyrolyse als festen Bestandteil der Kreislaufwirtschaft und der Dekarbonisierungsstrategie globaler Energieunternehmen zu etablieren.

title: VIEWPOINT: Japan aviation finance – deep liquidity meets complex risk
description:
While Japanese investors remain highly disciplined—typically favouring tier-one airline credits, high-quality assets and jurisdictions offering legal and geopolitical stability—the depth of liquidity has continued to expand.
One notable feature of the market is the increasing sophistication of both Japanese investors and international airlines accessing Japanese capital.
The aviation industry’s pathway towards decarbonisation is nevertheless different from that of many other infrastructure sectors.
Japanese investors are focused on country risk, airline credit quality, fuel-price volatility, sanctions exposure, repossession risk and whether the metal will remain liquid throughout the life cycle.
(Editor’s Note: Olivia Matsushita is a partner at Sidley Austin.)
text: Olivia Matsushita H1 2026 reinforced Japan’s position as one of the most important sources of equity capital for global transportation finance, with the Japanese operating lease (JOL) and Japanese operating lease with call option (JOLCO) markets continuing to underpin a significant volume of aircraft financings. While Japanese investors remain highly disciplined—typically favouring tier-one airline credits, high-quality assets and jurisdictions offering legal and geopolitical stability—the depth of liquidity has continued to expand. Despite heightened regional tensions, we have seen particularly strong demand for JOLCO financings involving UAE carriers over the past six months, demonstrating that well-structured transactions with strong credits continue to attract Japanese investor appetite. More broadly, JOL and JOLCO issuance has grown materially, driven by robust domestic investor demand and an increasing number of international airlines seeking to access the Japanese equity market. One notable feature of the market is the increasing sophistication of both Japanese investors and international airlines accessing Japanese capital. The JOL/JOLCO market is no longer viewed simply as an alternative source of aircraft financing. For many established airlines and lessors, Japan has become a strategic component of their broader funding programmes, providing access to a deep and differentiated pool of capital alongside conventional bank debt, operating leases and capital-markets financing. At the same time, the asset profile attracting Japanese investment is broadening. Narrowbody aircraft remain particularly attractive because of their global operator base and residual-value resilience, while high-quality widebody transactions continue to find lift where the underlying airline credit is strong. Investors are also increasingly looking at regional aircraft and aircraft engines as attractive assets that can offer a lower economical entry point into the aviation market. This diversification is significant. It enables Japanese investors to spread their aviation exposure across multiple assets, operators and lease maturities rather than concentrating capital in a single aircraft. It also requires investors to understand different risks: engine investments, for example, require considerably greater focus on maintenance condition, shop-visit exposure and remaining life of life-limited parts, while regional aircraft may present a smaller secondary operator pool and different remarketing considerations. Impact of power demand, AI, energy security, decarbonisation and geopolitics In transportation finance, these themes translate less into power-sector investment decisions and more into credit, asset and jurisdiction analysis. Decarbonisation is influencing fleet renewal, with Japanese airlines and global carriers prioritising more fuel-efficient aircraft and engines. The aviation industry’s pathway towards decarbonisation is nevertheless different from that of many other infrastructure sectors. There is no immediately scalable technological substitute for conventional commercial aircraft. Sustainable aviation fuel, improvements in engine efficiency and longer-term development of alternative propulsion technologies will play a role, but for the foreseeable future one of the most effective ways for airlines to reduce emissions per passenger is to replace older aircraft with newer, more fuel-efficient machines. This creates an interesting alignment between environmental objectives and aviation finance: fleet renewal requires enormous amounts of capital and Japanese equity is expected to continue to fuel this market. Aircraft and engine supply constraints are also reshaping financing decisions. OEM production delays, supply-chain challenges and lengthy engine maintenance turnaround times have restricted the availability of new and serviceable aircraft. Scarcity has supported aircraft values, lease rates and demand for spare engines and that trend is likely to continue for some time. Geopolitical uncertainty is another increasingly important factor. Japanese investors are focused on country risk, airline credit quality, fuel-price volatility, sanctions exposure, repossession risk and whether the metal will remain liquid throughout the life cycle. Recent geopolitical events have demonstrated that even a financially strong airline may be exposed to risks outside its direct control, including airspace closures, regional conflict, disruption to payment channels, rapidly changing sanctions regimes and changes in the availability or cost of war-risk insurance. This is beginning to influence legal documentation as well as investment decisions. Lessors and financiers are paying greater attention to whether the aircraft can continue to be operated, insured, maintained, moved and, if necessary, repossessed throughout the lease term. Geopolitical risk has therefore become an integral part of residual-value and credit analysis. H2 2026 and beyond Looking ahead, I expect Japan-related transportation finance activity to be shaped by four key themes: the continued deployment of Japanese capital into cross-border aircraft financings, persistent aircraft and engine supply constraints, ongoing fleet renewal programmes, and increasingly sophisticated risk allocation between stakeholders. Market participants will be closely monitoring the trajectory of interest rates and foreign-exchange movements and their impact on transaction economics and investor returns. At the same time, risk allocation among airlines, lenders, Japanese equity investors and other stakeholders will continue to evolve in response to a more complex macroeconomic and geopolitical environment. The prevailing expectation is that transaction volumes will remain robust through H2 2026 and beyond. Japan’s combination of deep domestic liquidity, sophisticated arrangers and longstanding relationships with the global airline and leasing community remains one of the market’s defining strengths and should continue to reinforce Japan’s position as a leading source of capital for the global aviation finance industry. text:
Jakarta, CNN Indonesia --

Perusahaan afiliasi milik konglomerat Prajogo Pangestu, Aster, resmi mengakuisisi saham Changi Airport Fuel Hydrant Installation, Singapura.

Langkah tersebut membawa Aster masuk ke dalam pasar bahan bakar penerbangan atau avtur sekaligus memperdalam investasi perusahaan di Singapura.

Aster kini bergabung dengan perusahaan energi besar lainnya dalam menyediakan avtur secara langsung kepada maskapai internasional di Bandara Changi yang berstatus sebagai salah satu pusat penerbangan tersibuk di dunia.

Pihak Aster tidak mengungkapkan secara rinci nilai transaksi kesepakatan ini. Proses akuisisi juga masih menunggu persetujuan dari regulator dan pemenuhan sejumlah persyaratan lainnya.

"Akusisi ini merupakan langkah penting dalam ekspansi Aster ke sektor bahan bakar penerbangan," ujar Deputy CEO Aster Andre Khor dikutip dari akun Instagram @forbesasia, Minggu (30/8).

Menurut dia, investasi ini akan digabungkan dengan kegiatan penyulingan, penyimpanan, serta kemampuan pengembangan sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) perusahaan.

Hal tersebut diharapkan mampu memperkuat posisi Aster dalam mendukung kebutuhan energi penerbangan di Singapura dan kawasan sekitarnya.

"Jika digabungkan dengan kegiatan penyulingan dan penyimpanan yang kami miliki serta kemampuan kami yang terus berkembang dalam memproduksi bahan bakar penerbangan berkelanjutan, investasi ini memperkuat posisi kami untuk mendukung kebutuhan energi penerbangan yang terus berkembang di Singapura dan kawasan sekitarnya, sekaligus melayani salah satu pusat penerbangan terkemuka di dunia," ujar Andre.

Aster merupakan perusahaan yang dimiliki Chandra Asri Group dan Glencore.

Pada 2025 lalu, kedua perusahaan tersebut mengakuisisi Shell Energy and Chemicals Park (SECP) di Singapura melalui perusahaan patungan CAPGC Pte. Ltd, yang sebagian besar dimiliki dan dioperasikan oleh Chandra Asri Group dengan Glencore memegang saham minoritas.

Kesepakatan tersebut diselesaikan melalui pembelian saham anak usaha Shell Singapore Pte. Ltd., yakni Aster Chemicals and Energy Pte. Ltd. (Aster).

Adapun PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) dimiliki oleh PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) sebesar 34,63 persen, di mana 71,37 persen saham BRPT dikendalikan langsung oleh Prajogo Pangestu.

Berdasarkan data Forbes, kekayaan Prajogo Pangestu mencapai US$17,2 miliar.

text:
Qantas Airways ((QABSY)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Qantas Airways struck a cautiously upbeat tone in its latest earnings call, highlighting strong cash generation, resilient profits and record customer metrics despite a sharp fuel shock from Middle East conflict and rising industry costs. Management stressed disciplined capital allocation and argued that heavy fleet investment today should translate into structurally higher margins and earnings over the medium term.

Resilient Profit Amid Geopolitical Fuel Shock

Qantas reported underlying profit before tax of A$2.064 billion for FY26, achieved even after a sizeable A$420 million hit from the Middle East conflict that drove up jet fuel costs and dampened regional demand. Executives framed the result as proof of the strength of Qantas’ integrated portfolio, with domestic, international and loyalty businesses collectively cushioning geopolitical volatility.

Strong Cash Flow and Solid Balance Sheet

Operating cash flow reached A$3.9 billion, underpinning a balance sheet that closed FY26 with net debt at A$6.2 billion, comfortably within the A$5.5–6.9 billion target range. Liquidity exceeds A$13 billion, giving the group scope to fund its heavy capex program while management aims to steer leverage back toward the middle of the target band by FY28.

Shareholder Payouts Continue via Base Dividends

Despite macro and cost headwinds, the board approved a final fully franked base dividend of A$300 million, taking total FY26 base dividends to A$600 million, or A$0.396 per share. In aggregate, about A$700 million was returned to shareholders during the year through dividends, signaling a commitment to ongoing distributions even as buybacks remain on hold.

Fleet Renewal Drives Investment and Efficiency

Qantas invested A$4.0 billion in FY26, with 29 aircraft joining the fleet, more than half being latest‑generation types such as the A321XLR, A220, A321LR and A320neo. Jetstar’s narrow‑body capacity is now roughly 50% new‑fleet, which management says is already delivering improved fuel efficiency, lower maintenance costs and higher customer satisfaction scores.

Record Customer Satisfaction and Operational Performance

Customer satisfaction reached its highest level in a decade, with Qantas Domestic NPS up seven points, Qantas International up five and Jetstar International up six. Operationally, Qantas achieved 85% on‑time departures in June, making it the best‑performing major global airline for that month and reinforcing its pitch as a premium, reliable carrier.

Domestic and Jetstar Segments Deliver Strong Earnings

Group Domestic posted EBIT of A$1.44 billion, translating to a healthy 13% margin, while Jetstar Domestic revenue rose 11% on just 4% capacity growth, showing strong demand and pricing power. Jetstar Australia International contributed EBIT of A$279 million with an 11% operating margin, underscoring the importance of the low‑cost brand within the portfolio.

Loyalty Business Continues to Grow and Diversify

Qantas Loyalty delivered underlying EBIT of A$625 million, up 12% year on year, with points earned and redeemed both increasing by 9%. The unit reported record reward seat bookings and has now enrolled one in four Australian SMEs in Qantas Business Rewards, reinforcing loyalty as a recurring earnings engine with attractive growth prospects.

Transformation Savings Outpace Cost Inflation

The company’s transformation program generated A$455 million in savings during FY26, exceeding prior guidance and partially offsetting inflationary pressures. Management highlighted these savings as critical in managing CPI‑linked expenses and other cost growth, positioning Qantas to defend margins while it absorbs near‑term fleet and EIS charges.

International Fleet Strategy Targets Margin Upside

Qantas International is targeting a path to a 10% EBIT margin by FY31, underpinned by the rollout of A350s, 787s and the Project Sunrise ultra‑long‑haul strategy. Project Sunrise alone is expected to add around A$400 million in earnings by FY31, while retirement of the A380 fleet should unlock an estimated A$300 million net cashflow benefit between FY28 and FY31.

Fuel Hedging and Revenue Levers for FY27

The group has hedged about 85% of Brent exposure for the first half of FY27, with H1 fuel costs guided at roughly A$3.6 billion based on market jet fuel of A$197 per barrel. Management expects total revenue per ASK to rise 8–10% for both domestic and international operations, relying on fares, ancillary revenue and load factor optimization to counter mounting fuel and cost pressures.

Sustainability Initiatives Gain Traction

Sustainable aviation fuel procurement increased to 1.1% of total fuel usage in FY26, marking gradual progress toward lower‑carbon operations. Qantas also committed A$30 million to carbon removal projects and published an expanded climate and transition sustainability report, signaling that decarbonization is being embedded into long‑term strategic planning.

Capital Recycling and Portfolio Optimization

The group flagged the divestment of its stake in Jetstar Japan as a key step in capital recycling, redeploying funds into higher‑return opportunities. This move fits into a broader strategy to sharpen focus on core markets and optimize capital allocation across the network, especially as capex ramps up with the incoming fleet.

Profit, EPS and Cost Pressures Weigh on Results

Underlying EPS fell to A$0.96, down 13% versus FY25, while underlying PBT was A$330 million lower year on year, largely reflecting the A$420 million Middle East impact. Higher fuel costs added A$492 million, including A$26 million of extra gross carbon charges, pushing unit costs ex‑fuel up 4.1% against a 3.6% rise in unit revenue, highlighting that costs are currently growing faster than revenue.

Statutory Profit Dampened by One‑off Charges

Statutory profit after tax came in at A$1.289 billion, a decline of A$316 million compared with FY25 as several one‑off items weighed on the bottom line. These included the closure of Jetstar Asia and legal provisions associated with class action settlement, which management framed as necessary clean‑up costs to reset the portfolio and risk profile.

Share Buyback Paused in Favour of Reinvestment

The previously announced A$150 million on‑market share buyback has been paused and will not go ahead, with Qantas prioritizing reinvestment in the business. Executives argued that directing capital to fleet renewal and strategic projects offers better long‑term returns than buybacks at this stage of the cycle, even as base dividends remain intact.

Short‑Term Earnings Drag from Fleet and EIS Costs

Accelerated fleet investment pushed depreciation and amortization up by A$236 million in FY26, with additional entry‑into‑service costs of about A$150 million expected across FY28–29 as new aircraft come online. Management acknowledged these charges will weigh on near‑term earnings but maintains they are the price of securing future efficiency gains, capacity and margin expansion.

Middle East Conflict and Industry Costs Add Pressure

The Middle East conflict generated an estimated A$420 million net impact in Q4 FY26 through higher fuel prices and weaker local confidence, underscoring Qantas’ exposure to global energy markets. Beyond fuel, other industry expenses including airport, security and government charges rose by around A$95 million, adding another layer of cost pressure that the group must offset through productivity and pricing.

Guidance Points to Revenue Growth and Ongoing Investment

Looking ahead, management expects group TRASK to increase 8–10% in H1 FY27 for both domestic and international segments, supported by pricing and capacity discipline, while H1 fuel expense is guided at around A$3.6 billion with hedging in place. Capex is forecast at A$4.3–4.6 billion in FY27 with up to 31 aircraft deliveries, Qantas Loyalty EBIT is guided to grow 5–7% and remains on track for A$800 million to A$1 billion by FY30, and Qantas International is still targeting a 10% EBIT margin by FY31 with Project Sunrise contributing roughly A$400 million of uplift.

Qantas’ latest earnings call paints a picture of a carrier leaning hard into transformation and fleet renewal while navigating a tricky mix of fuel shocks and rising structural costs. For investors, the story is one of solid cash flow, sustained dividends and clear medium‑term upside, tempered by near‑term margin pressure as the capex cycle and geopolitical volatility run their course.

text:
India’s sustainable aviation fuel industry could reach cost parity with conventional jet fuel by 2036, a report said. Domestic production using agricultural residue and renewable power could reduce exposure to currency fluctuations and imported crude prices, while accounting for health and carbon benefits could potentially bring parity forward.

Key Highlights:

India’s SAF could achieve cost parity by 2036.

Domestic production can reduce currency and import risks.

Agricultural residue and renewable power can support SAF.

Health and carbon benefits could accelerate cost parity.

New Delhi, Aug 29: India’s sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) industry could achieve cost parity with conventional jet fuel by 2036, according to a report. The assessment suggests that evaluating SAF economics over a project’s full 25-year operating period provides a more favourable outlook than comparing single-year production costs.

Power-and-biomass-to-liquids (PBtL) fuel is estimated to cost $1.42 per litre in 2030, compared with $0.97 per litre for conventional jet fuel. However, the gap narrows significantly when long-term costs are considered, with a 2030-commissioned PBtL plant estimated to have a levelised cost of around Rs 127 per litre.

Domestic SAF production could also provide greater protection against currency volatility and global commodity price fluctuations. Historical data showed wholesale jet fuel prices rising around 5% annually in nominal rupee terms between 2005 and 2025, partly due to dollar-denominated commodity inflation and rupee depreciation.

India’s agricultural residues and low-cost renewable electricity could support a domestic SAF ecosystem while reducing reliance on imported crude oil. Researchers estimate that new synthetic fuel plants commissioned in 2036 could achieve full levelised cost parity, while monetising avoided health and carbon costs could potentially bring commercial parity as early as 2030.

text:
Niutech's Game-Changing Entry in SAF Production

On an ordinary day in Jinan, China, Niutech Technology Group Co., Ltd decided it wasn't going to be just another player on the sideline anymore. They've just inked a deal with one of the big boys, a global energy major, pushing their industrial continuous pyrolysis technology into the big leagues of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) production.

Cracking the SAF Code

For the uninitiated, this isn't just another industrial gig. We're talking about a process where waste plastic, that pesky modern plague, gets converted into something aviation actually needs—SAF. As more countries shove regulations down the aviation industry's throat, calling for SAF to compose 70% of fuel by 2050 under EU mandates, we're staring at a brewing storm of demand. Niutech steps right in, saying, "We've got your feedstock crisis sorted." This isn't mere bluster; this is a lifeline to industries running amok for alternatives to used cooking oil.

Partners in Decarbonization

Speaking of alternatives, Niutech's tech can handle grungy plastics without sweating the small stuff like shredding or sorting. That's a huge win. They’ve shown they can take the yucky stuff—PP, PE, PS, ABS, nylon—and turn them into gold. Or oil, in this case, ready for the big leagues of SAF production.

"Large-scale pyrolysis projects place demanding requirements on the continuous operation capability of the equipment," noted a Niutech market exec, sipping in the sweet moment of recognition.

The Strategic Footprint Expanded

Niutech’s been quietly working away, their equipment already churning in high-demand markets like the UK and South Korea. This partnership, though, marks something new—a finger in the pie of a global energy giant's supply chain, supplying them with the machinery needed to convert their massive refineries to the SAF-producing powerhouse.

Niutech's continuous operation capacity stands at 10,000 to 50,000 tons per year.

Countries with enacted SAF mandates: EU, UK, Singapore, and counting.

The valorization of waste plastic as a second option for SAF feedstock.

How Sustainable is This Leap?

This isn’t just about churning profit from heaps of plastic; it’s a seismic shift toward cleaner skies. The aviation sector, a notorious polluter, is in desperate need of a redux, and Niutech’s pyrolysis solutions might just be the missing piece in the grand puzzle of decarbonizing flights. Not to be corny, but their 40 years in the game, perfecting this tech, speaks volumes. The world may still need convincing, but Niutech's placing their bets squarely on being pioneers of change.

Niutech: A Force to Watch

There’s something inherently satisfying about an underdog stepping onto the main stage. Niutech’s stock (688309) has seen some solid action, thanks in part to their broadening clientele and groundbreaking tech—all proving their seat at the global energy table is well-deserved. If you’re watching the environmental tech space, keep your eyes peeled because Niutech’s journey is far from over—but the stakes just got a whole lot higher.

Investors, regulators, and industry players alike should be perking up at this development. As the clock ticks louder on climate commitments, Niutech’s solution might not just turn waste into profit; it could catapult aviation fuel into a cleaner future.

‘साखर पेटली’, 'साखर कडाडली', 'साखर कडू झाली' या आणि अशा मथळ्यांच्या बातम्यांनी संपूर्ण देशातील वातावरण ढवळून निघालं आहे. देशभरात साखरेच्या दरात अचानक झालेल्या वाढीमुळे केवळ सरकारच नव्हे, तर साखर उद्योगाशी निगडीत सर्वच घटक जसे की, साखर उत्पादक, साखर व्यापारी, साखर ग्राहक, ऊस उत्पादक शेतकरी, साखर उद्योगाला वित्त पुरवठा करणाऱ्या बँका हे सर्वजण आश्चर्यचकित झाले आणि संभ्रमात पडले आहेत. या 'न भुतो न भविष्यति' अशा ऐतिहासिक घटनेच्या मुळाशी जाऊन एकूणच साखर उद्योगाबाबतची वस्तुस्थिती प्रांजळ आणि पारदर्शक माहिती माझ्या २७ वर्षांच्या प्रदीर्घ अनुभवावर आधारित एका तटस्थ भूमिकेतून या लेखाद्वारे मांडण्याचा हा एक प्रयत्न आहे. चुक भूल देणे घेणे!

आपल्या देशातील साखरेचा दरडोई दरसालचा खप २० किलो इतका आहे. एका चौकोनी कुटुंबाचा (आई, वडील, दोन अपत्ये) महिन्याचा साखरेचा असणारा ६.६ किलो वापराचा खर्च ४३३.३३ रुपये इतकाच आहे. तो बिसलेरी पाण्याच्या बाटलीवरील खर्चापेक्षाही कमी आहे. या वस्तुस्थ‍ितीच्या पार्श्वभूमीवर केवळ साखरेच्या भाववाढीवर होणारी टीका आणि गदारोळ अनाकलनीय आहे. जागतिक स्तरावर वार्षिक २८५ लाख टन साखरेचा खप असणारा आपला देश साखर उत्पादनात अग्रस्थानी आहे; मात्र यातील सुमारे ६५ टक्के साखरेचा खप हा औद्योगिक क्षेत्रातून होतो. यात मिठाई, शीतपेये, चॉकलेट, आईस्क्रीम बिस्किटे, औषधांच्या गोळ्या यांचे दर जेव्हा साखर दरात घसरण होते व ते नीचांकी पातळीवर जातात तेव्हा कमी होत नाहीत. ते वाढलेल्या दरावरच टिकून राहतात आणि याबाबत कधी कुठे, चर्चा टीका होत नाही; मात्र साखर दरातील वाढीवर सर्व स्तरांतूून टोकाची आणि धारदार टीका होते. वास्तविकत: साखरेची निर्मिती शेतातील उभ्या उसात होते. ज्या उसाची जोपासना एकर-दोन एकर क्षेत्र असणाऱ्या अल्पभूधारक शेतकऱ्याकडून उन्हा-पावसात, थंडीत जीवापाड मेहनत करून होत असते. वर्षभरापेक्षा जास्त काळ जोपासलेल्या उसाला साखर दरवाढीतून दोन पैसे जास्त मिळाल्यास इतका तळतळाट का होतो? त्याच्या झोपडीतील स्वयंपाकघरात गोडधोड जेवण आणि मुलांच्या अंगावर चांगले कपडे, चांगले शिक्षण मिळाल्यास त्याचे दु:ख का व्हावे, या प्रश्नाचे उत्तर मला अजूनही मिळालेले नाही.

जगात भारत असा एकमेव देश आहे, जिथे ऊस आणि साखर हे केंद्र शासनाच्या अत्यावश्यक वस्तू कायदा [Essential Commodity Act] यांच्या बंधनात जखडलेले आहेत. या ECA कायद्याच्या उल्लंघनाविरुद्ध थेट फौजदारी गुन्हा दाखल होऊ शकतो. याच्या आधारावर केंद्र शासनातील अन्न मंत्रालयाने उसाचा किमान दर, साखरेचा किमान विक्री दर, साखरेचा महिनानिहाय विक्री कोटा देशभरातील सर्व ५३५ साखर कारखान्यांना कायद्याने बंधनकारक केला आहे. देशातील या सुमारे दीड लाख कोटी रुपयांची वार्ष‍िक उलाढाल असणाऱ्या दोन क्रमांकाच्या कृषी उद्योगाशी जवळपास ५ कोटी ऊस उत्पादक शेतकरी, १५ लाख कर्मचारी, ८ लाख उसतोड मजूर निगडीत आहेत. या उद्योगातून शासनाला वर्षागणिक १५ हजार कोटी रुपयांचा महसूल मिळतो. अशा या ग्रामीण भारताची नाळ असणाऱ्या महत्त्वपूर्ण उद्योगाची ECA कायद्यांच्या जोखडातून सुटका होणे जरुरीचे आहे, तरच हा उद्योग मोकळेपणाने श्वास घेऊ शकेल आणि स्वावलंबी होऊ शकेल. भारताने स्वीकारेलल्या मुक्त अर्थव्यवस्थेला खऱ्याअर्थाने न्याय मिळेल, असे वाटते.

भारतातील आणि विशेषतः महाराष्ट्रातील साखर उद्योग एका महत्त्वाच्या आणि निर्णायक वळणावर आलेला आहे. वैयक्तिक कारखान्यांनी गाळप क्षमतेमध्ये केलेल्या वाढीमुळे गाळप हंगामाचे दिवस १५०-१६० वरून शंभराच्या खाली आले आहेत. त्यामुळे कारखान्यांचे अर्थचक्र पूर्णपणे कोलमडू शकते. त्यासाठी 'कल्पतरू' असणाऱ्या उसाची मुबलक उपलब्धता असणे अत्यंत महत्त्वाचे ठरणार आहे. देशपातळीवर उसाखालील असलेल्या ५६-५७ लाख हेक्टर क्षेत्रात वाढ होण्याची शक्यता नाही आणि उसाची हेक्टरी ७५-८० टनांची उत्पादकतादेखील गोठली आहे. त्यामुळेच मर्यादित क्षेत्रातून जास्तीत जास्त उसाची उपलब्धता करवून घेण्यावरच साखर उद्योगाचे भवितव्य अवलंबून असणार आहे. या पार्श्वभूमीवर Centre of Excellence च्या माध्यमातून उसाच्या नवीन वाणांची उपलब्धता ४ ते ६ वर्षे कालावधीत होणे, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्तेच्या नव्या तंत्रज्ञानाचा ऊस उत्पादनवाढीसाठी अवलंब करणे, आणि या 'कल्पतरू' उसाच्या शेंड्यापासून बुडक्यापर्यंतच्या भागावर मूल्यावर्धन करून साखरेव्यतिरिक्त इथेनॉल, सहवीज, CBG, Green Hydrogen आणि विमानाचे इंधन (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) अशी विविध नवनवी उत्पादने नजीकच्या भविष्यात तयार करण्याशिवाय गत्यंतर नाही.

कारखान्यांनीदेखील भविष्यातील उभी ठाकणारी आव्हाने आणि त्यात दडलेल्या संधी यांचा अभ्यास करून आपापले वार्षिक कार्य आराखडे तयार करून त्याची अंमलबजावणी करणे आवश्यक आहे. अर्थशास्त्राच्या मूलमंत्राचा 'A Rupee Saved is a Rupee earned' म्हणजेच 'एक रुपयाची बचत ही त्या रुपयाची मिळकत असते' या मंत्राचे काटेकोर पालन करणे गरजेचे आहे. महाराष्ट्रातील कारखान्यांनी बॅंकेच्या कर्जावर अतिअवलंबित न राहता स्वनिधी निर्माण करण्यावर भर द्यावा, जेणेकरून व्याजांच्या बोजाखाली दबलेले अर्थचक्र फिरू शकेल. कारखाना प्रक्रियेमध्ये Automation आणि Mechanization मोठ्या प्रमाणावर अवलंबले पाहिजे आणि कारखानदारी ही व्यावसायिक भूमिकेने चालवली पाहिजे. व्यावसायिक निपुणता (Professional Management) आणि आक्रमक विपणन प्रणाली (Aggressive Marketing) अवलंबून आपली आर्थिक परिस्थिती मजबूत करण्यावर पूर्ण लक्ष केंद्रित करणे आवश्यक आहे. त्यासाठी जिथे जिथे अद्ययावत Training उपलब्ध असेल तिथे तिथे जाऊन ते आत्मसात केल्याशिवाय तरणोपाय नाही हे निश्चित आहे. ऊस, साखर, इथेनॉल, सहवीज हे सर्व विषय केंद्र शासनाच्या अखत्यारित येतात.

या बाबतची धोरणे आणि निर्णय केंद्र शासनातील ५-६ मंत्र्याच्या मंत्री गटाच्या स्तरावरून अंतिम होतात. केंद्रीय गृह आणि सहकार मंत्री अमित शहा यांच्या अध्यक्षते खालील या मंत्री गटात केंद्रीय अन्न मंत्री, पेट्रोलियम मंत्री, वित्त मंत्री, कृषी मंत्री आणि वाणीज्य मंत्री यांचा समावेश आहे. मात्र निर्णय अंतिम स्तरावर येण्यापुर्वी विषयाची टिपणी १२ केंद्रिय सचीवांच्या समिती कडून अभ्यासली जाते व त्यानंतर Inter-Ministerial Committee च्या स्तरावर तपासली जाते मूळ टिपणी तयार करण्यापुर्वी केंद्रशासनातील संबंधीत विभागाकडून देशातील सहकारी साखर उद्योगाशी शिखर संस्था(National Coop. Sugar Federation) आणि खाजगी साखर कारखान्यांची शिखर संस्था (ISMA) यांच्याशी अनौपचारिक चर्चा करण्याचा एक स्तुत्य उपक्रम राबविल जातो. या चर्चे दरम्यान आम्ही वेळोवेळी साखर उद्योगाला जमिनी स्तरावर भेडसावणाऱ्या समस्या आणि आव्हाने शासनासमोर मांडत असतो. त्यातल्या काही मान्य होतात आणि काही प्रलंबीत राहतात. ऊसाचा दर हा साखरेच्या किमान विक्री दराशी जोडला जावा तसेच इथेनॉलचे खरेदी दर कच्चा मालाच्या दराशी व उत्पादन खर्चाशी निगडीत असावेत या व अशा विविध मागण्यांचा केंद्रीय मंत्री गटाकडून लवकरात लवकर निपटारा होणे निकडीचे आहे.

जाता जाता मला अल निनोरुपी अस्मानी संकटा विषयी गांभीर्यपुर्वक जाणीव करून द्यावीशी वाटते. फेब्रुवारी २०२६ पासूनच जगातील सर्वच हवामान तज्ञ आणि संस्थाकडून अलनिनोच्या संभाव्य संकटाची जाणीव जाहीरपणे करण्यात आली. अल निनो चा प्रभाव अंदाजानुसार जगभरात आखडते पाऊसमान ते अतिवृष्टीच्या रुपात अनुभवास आला त्याचा काहीसा अनुकुल परिणाम ऊस पिकवणाऱ्या राज्यांतून अनुभवास मिळाला. जून –जुलै मधील अतिवृष्टीमुळे राज्यात उभ्या असलेल्या ऊसाच्या वाढीला उपयोग झाला आणि प्रमुख धरणांच्या पाणलोट क्षेत्रात पाण्याचे समाधान कारक साठे झाले आहेत. मात्र सप्टेंबर ते डिसेंबर २०२६ दरम्यान च्या चार महिन्याच्या काळात Super EL NINO चा जबरदस्त दणका दिसणार असल्याचे तज्ञांचे भाकित आहे. ते खरे ठरल्यास नव्या लागणीवर आणि ऊसाच्या खोडव्यावर अत्यंत प्रतिकुल परिणाम होऊ शकतो आणि त्याच्या फल स्वरूप हंगाम २०२७-२८ मध्ये ऊसाची उपलब्धता कमी राहील्यास कारखान्या समोर प्रचंड संकट उभे राहू शकते. तशी परिस्थिती उदभवल्यास केंद्र शासनाकडून आयातीद्वारे साखरेची उपलब्धता करता येवू शकते. पण गाळपावीना राहीलेल्या कारखांन्याची अवस्था कशी असणार आहे याची कल्पनाही करवत नाही.

अर्थात आपण सर्वजणच प्रार्थना करुयात कि तशी आणीबाणीची परिस्थ‍िती उदभवू नये आणि काही चमत्कार होऊन अलनिनोचा प्रभाव कमी होऊन ला निनो येवो व शेतात मुबलक पाऊस पडो.

title: Thyssenkrupp's Rally Holds Its Ground: A Green Hydrogen Setback Meets a Defence Windfall

text:
The conglomerate's summer momentum is proving remarkably resilient. Even as its hydrogen division abandons plans for mass production of a key electrolysis technology — a retreat that carries a €30 million one-time charge — the shares continue to trade within striking distance of their 52-week peak, buoyed by a record defence order book and tangible progress in the steel business.

Thyssenkrupp Nucera, the group's green hydrogen arm, has decided against investing in its own large-scale manufacturing of SOEC stacks, a critical component for electrolysis. The decision, taken roughly a fortnight ago, triggered the impairment charge in the fourth quarter and forced a downward revision to the division's earnings outlook. Management now guides for an EBIT loss of between €105 million and €75 million for fiscal 2025/26, a noticeably wider deficit than the €80 million-to-€30 million range previously communicated. Revenue expectations for the green hydrogen segment have also been trimmed, with the company now pencilling in €100 million to €130 million rather than the earlier €120 million-to-€170 million projection.

The pullback underscores a broader industry reality: scaling up industrial manufacturing capacity in hydrogen remains fraught, a challenge that has tripped up other players in the sector as well. Weak order intake at Nucera — just €81 million in the third quarter — had already prompted the company to slash the upper end of its full-year order forecast from €850 million to €670 million. Berenberg responded on 25 August by cutting its revenue and earnings estimates for the 2026 through 2028 period, though the research house kept its "Hold" rating on the stock intact.

Within the context of the wider group, however, the Nucera drag looks manageable. The recently raised group-level EBIT guidance — the lower bound was lifted from €500 million to €600 million around two weeks ago — pertains to the conglomerate's adjusted earnings and is not threatened by the comparatively small hydrogen segment.

Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Thyssenkrupp?

The market's reaction has been telling. Thyssenkrupp shares closed Friday at €14.67, a modest 1.2 percent dip on the day, yet the weekly gain stands at 9.2 percent and the 30-day advance at 23 percent. The stock now sits just 3.4 percent below its 52-week high of €15.18, reached on 28 August. That strength has been driven primarily by the upgraded corporate outlook and a series of analyst upgrades, with the Nucera disappointment doing little to dent investor confidence in a group that spans steel, marine systems, and materials trading.

Supporting the bullish narrative, Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems (TKMS) reported an order book of €20.1 billion after nine months of the current fiscal year — a figure expected to surpass €25 billion once an anticipated frigate programme is factored in. The group retains a 51 percent majority stake in the naval subsidiary, which was listed in October 2025, and the twelve-month lock-up period on that holding expires in October 2026, a date investors will watch closely for potential changes to the ownership structure.

In the steel division, Thyssenkrupp Steel has granted final acceptance to partner Primetals Technologies for the new continuous caster No. 4 at the Duisburg site. The facility, designed for high-margin premium steel grades, represents a concrete step in the company's shift toward higher-value products. Meanwhile, the Carbon2Chem research project is advancing hydrogen infrastructure for Nucera in Duisburg, alongside plans for a sustainable aviation fuel plant — evidence that long-term transformation initiatives remain on track despite the strained core business.

The Nucera retreat fits into a broader pattern of portfolio reorganisation. An extraordinary general meeting in early August approved the carve-out of the tk accelis division, and the hydrogen decision demonstrates that even growth areas are not immune to course corrections when market conditions or technology pathways shift. For investors, the key question remains whether the group can deliver on its August guidance — and while the Nucera charges are unlikely to be decisive, the volatility in new technology segments serves as a reminder of how uneven the earnings trajectory can be. With the TKMS lock-up expiry on the horizon, the coming months will test whether the conglomerate's restructuring story can keep pace with its share price.

text:
Synthetic jet fuel made without crude oil

UK clean-fuel start-up Zero Petroleum is moving closer to commercial-scale production of synthetic aviation fuel after successfully demonstrating a fuel designed to replicate conventional Jet A-1. The company produces the fuel using green hydrogen and captured carbon dioxide instead of crude oil, offering another potential pathway for reducing aviation’s dependence on fossil fuels. The technology falls within the growing Power-to-Liquid (PtL) sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) sector, which uses renewable electricity to create liquid fuels from hydrogen and carbon. Zero Petroleum is now advancing plans for its first commercial-scale facility as it works to move the technology beyond demonstration production.

Synthetic jet fuel made without crude oil

Zero Petroleum’s process begins with green hydrogen generated using renewable electricity. The hydrogen is combined with captured carbon dioxide and converted through a series of synthesis and upgrading stages into synthetic hydrocarbons. These hydrocarbons can then be refined into aviation fuel with chemical and physical properties designed to match those of conventional Jet A-1. Instead of extracting petroleum from underground, the production pathway relies primarily on renewable electricity, water and captured carbon as its inputs. This could significantly reduce dependence on fossil-based feedstocks if the technology is successfully deployed at scale. The company says its demonstration program has shown that synthetic Jet A-1 can be produced using this approach, marking an important step toward larger-scale PtL fuel manufacturing.

Drop-in fuel could support aviation decarbonization

A major focus of Zero Petroleum’s development program is compatibility with the aviation sector’s existing equipment and infrastructure. Rather than creating an entirely new type of fuel that would require extensive modifications to aircraft, engines or airport systems, the company is developing a synthetic alternative intended to replicate conventional Jet A-1. This “drop-in” approach could be important for accelerating sustainable aviation fuel adoption. Aircraft fleets typically remain in operation for decades, while replacing airport fuel-storage and distribution infrastructure would require substantial investment. Synthetic fuels that can work with existing systems therefore offer a potential way to lower lifecycle emissions without requiring the aviation industry to replace its entire physical infrastructure.

Zero Petroleum plans first commercial-scale plant

Following its fuel demonstration, Zero Petroleum is progressing toward the development of its first commercial-scale synthetic aviation fuel facility. Key details about the proposed plant have not yet been publicly confirmed, including its final location, production capacity, investment cost and construction timeline. The next phase is expected to focus on scaling the production technology, completing engineering work and securing the financing and supply arrangements needed for commercial operations. Building a large PtL facility will require considerably more than the core fuel-production technology. Supporting infrastructure could include renewable electricity generation or supply, electrolyzers for green hydrogen, carbon dioxide capture or delivery systems, synthesis equipment, fuel upgrading facilities, storage capacity and export infrastructure. Reliable access to renewable power and water will also be critical to the economics and environmental performance of the project.

Power-to-liquid SAF targets aviation’s fossil fuel dependence

Aviation is considered one of the most challenging sectors to decarbonize because large commercial aircraft require fuels with high energy density, making direct electrification difficult for many medium- and long-haul routes. Power-to-Liquid fuels could help address this challenge by converting renewable energy into energy-dense liquid hydrocarbons suitable for aviation. When green hydrogen is produced with renewable electricity and the carbon used in fuel production comes from appropriate captured sources, synthetic aviation fuel has the potential to reduce lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions compared with conventional fossil jet fuel. The approach could also allow airlines to continue operating existing aircraft while gradually replacing petroleum-derived jet fuel with lower-carbon alternatives.

Scaling synthetic aviation fuel remains the next challenge

Zero Petroleum’s move toward commercial production highlights the transition now taking place across the sustainable aviation fuel industry: from proving that alternative fuels can be produced to demonstrating that they can be manufactured economically at industrial scale. Large PtL projects require substantial amounts of renewable electricity, hydrogen-production capacity and carbon dioxide, while their commercial viability depends heavily on production costs, financing and reliable access to low-carbon energy. If Zero Petroleum successfully scales its technology, its planned commercial facility could provide another demonstration of how green hydrogen and captured carbon can be transformed into synthetic aviation fuel without conventional crude oil. For an aviation industry searching for practical ways to cut its climate impact while continuing to use existing aircraft and infrastructure, synthetic Jet A-1 could become an increasingly important part of the long-term SAF market.

text:
New Delhi, Aug 29 (IANS) India's sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) industry could achieve cost parity with conventional jet fuel by 2036 with domestic production offering greater protection from currency fluctuations and global commodity price volatility, a report has said.

The report by Gulf Times said that evaluating SAF projects only through single-year production costs gives an incomplete picture of their long-term economics.

It noted that while power-and-biomass-to-liquids (PBtL) fuel is estimated to cost $1.42 per litre in 2030, compared with $0.97 per litre for conventional jet fuel, the gap narrows substantially when costs are assessed over a 25-year project cycle.

In addition, historical data between 2005 and 2025 showed wholesale jet fuel prices rising by 5 per cent annually in nominal rupee terms.

About 1.9 per cent of the increase was attributed to US dollar commodity inflation, while 3.1 per cent reflected rupee depreciation against the dollar.

According to the report, domestic synthetic fuel plants can help reduce this currency vulnerability as major operational inputs can be secured through long-term, rupee-denominated power purchase agreements at fixed tariffs.

Taking these dynamics into account, researchers estimated the levelised cost of PBtL fuel from a plant commissioned in 2030 at Rs 127 per litre, only 18 per cent above the adjusted levelised purchase cost of conventional jet fuel over the same 25-year period.

Under base-case market assumptions, new synthetic fuel facilities commissioned in 2036 are projected to achieve full levelised cost parity with conventional fuel, the report said.

It also noted that the cost gap could close sooner if the wider economic benefits of green fuel are factored into policy decisions.

Moreover, monetising health benefits from reduced agricultural field burning could add an estimated $0.38 per litre in avoided societal costs, while applying carbon costs could add up to $0.22 per litre.

These benefits could potentially bring SAF to commercial cost parity with conventional jet fuel as early as 2030, it said.

Additionally, the report highlighted the potential for India's agricultural residue and low-cost renewable power to support a domestic SAF ecosystem while reducing exposure to imported crude oil and foreign exchange risks.

--IANS

text:
JAKARTA, iNews.id - Aster, perusahaan yang dikendalikan orang terkaya kedua di Indonesia Prajogo Pangestu, melalui Chandra Asri Pacific, sepakat mengakuisisi saham Changi Airport Fuel Hydrant Installation (CAFHI). Transaksi tersebut menandai langkah Aster masuk ke bisnis bahan bakar penerbangan di Singapura.

Melansir Forbes, Aster menjelaskan bahwa akuisisi tersebut akan memungkinkan perusahaan bergabung dengan sejumlah perusahaan energi besar lainnya dalam memasok bahan bakar pesawat secara langsung kepada maskapai internasional di Bandara Changi.

Bandara Changi merupakan salah satu pusat penerbangan tersibuk di dunia.

Aster tidak mengungkapkan nilai transaksi tersebut. Akuisisi masih menunggu persetujuan regulator serta pemenuhan sejumlah persyaratan lainnya.

"Akuisisi ini merupakan langkah penting dalam ekspansi Aster ke bisnis bahan bakar penerbangan," kata Wakil Direktur Utama Aster yang berbasis di Singapura, Andre Khor dalam keterangannya dikutip, Sabtu (29/8/2026).

Menurutnya, langkah ini melengkapi bisnis pengolahan dan penyimpanan energi Aster serta kemampuan perusahaan yang terus berkembang di bidang sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) atau bahan bakar penerbangan berkelanjutan.

"Hal ini memperkuat posisi kami untuk mendukung kebutuhan energi penerbangan yang terus berkembang di Singapura dan kawasan, dalam melayani salah satu pusat penerbangan terkemuka di dunia," tuturnya.

Investasi di CAFHI melengkapi ekspansi Aster di bisnis SAF. Pada November, Aster bermitra dengan Aether Fuels untuk mengembangkan fasilitas produksi SAF di Pulau Bukom, kawasan pusat pengolahan minyak Singapura.

Fasilitas tersebut ditargetkan mulai beroperasi secara komersial pada 2028. Pabrik itu nantinya memiliki kapasitas produksi hingga 50 barel SAF per hari, atau sekitar 2.000 ton per tahun.

Aster juga bekerja sama dengan divisi infrastruktur Keppel untuk mengembangkan fasilitas SAF berbasis konversi etanol menjadi bahan bakar penerbangan di Jurong Island.

Langkah masuk ke bisnis avtur tersebut dilakukan ketika Aster semakin memperluas bisnisnya di Singapura.

Akuisisi saham CAFHI dilakukan hanya sekitar sepekan setelah Chandra Asri sepakat membeli bisnis dealer mobil milik Jardine Cycle & Carriage di Malaysia dan Singapura senilai 265 juta dolar Singapura atau sekitar 208 juta dolar AS.

Transaksi tersebut menjadi langkah pertama Chandra Asri masuk ke sektor otomotif. Perusahaan yang tercatat di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) itu juga terus memperbesar investasinya di Singapura.

Pada April 2025, Chandra Asri bersama perusahaan komoditas Glencore mengakuisisi aset kilang dan petrokimia milik Shell di negara tersebut.

Lima bulan kemudian, grup tersebut kembali melakukan ekspansi dengan membeli jaringan stasiun pengisian bahan bakar Esso di Singapura.

Aster merupakan bagian dari Chandra Asri yang dikendalikan Barito Pacific. Perusahaan yang awalnya bergerak di sektor kayu tersebut kemudian ditransformasi Prajogo Pangestu menjadi kelompok usaha energi dan petrokimia.

Prajogo Pangestu merupakan orang terkaya kedua di Indonesia. Berdasarkan data real-time Forbes, kekayaannya mencapai sekitar 16,9 miliar dolar AS atau setara Rp300 triliun (kurs Rp17.756 per dolar AS)

Selain bisnis energi dan petrokimia, kepentingan bisnis Prajogo juga mencakup perusahaan pertambangan batu bara Petrindo Jaya Kreasi, yang melantai di BEI pada 2023.

Ekspansi ke bisnis bahan bakar penerbangan di Singapura semakin memperluas portofolio bisnis Prajogo Pangestu di sektor energi sekaligus memperkuat kehadiran grupnya di salah satu pusat penerbangan utama Asia.
